original_title: Nitrile Oxide Annulation of π‐Dipolarophiles by Visible Light Organophotoredox Catalysis
title: Isoxazoles without a metal doing the catalyzing
blurb: Nitrile oxide [3+2] annulation run entirely on visible-light organophotoredox catalysis to build isoxazoles and isoxazolines, the usual metal photocatalyst swapped out for a purely organic one. Greener on paper, and apparently nobody had closed this particular loop yet.

original_title: Comprehensive synthesis of K48/K63 ubiquitin pentamers by graph-empowered automation
title: Covering all 56 ways to wire up a ubiquitin chain
blurb: K48/K63 ubiquitin chains have a combinatorial explosion of possible linkages that's made them a pain to prepare systematically. Pairing protected ubiquitin monomer synthesis with graph-based encoding and automation gets comprehensive access to all 56 K48/K63-linked tetramers and pentamers, not just whichever few someone made by hand before.

original_title: Enhancing Pharmaceutical Production with Scaled-Up Laser-Driven Annular Photoreactors
title: Scaling up photochemistry by keeping the laser out of the room
blurb: A kilogram-scale annular photoreactor grown from a 0.5W fiber prototype to roughly 8x the volume and about 1600x the optical power, now via an 800W diode laser. Piping the light in through a fiber keeps the hot, electrical parts away from the hazardous chemistry, which is what actually lets it run in an ATEX-rated plant.

original_title: Structure-Dependent Dual Regulation of Oxidative Stability and Protein Cross-Linking in Roasted Beef Patties: Potential Involvement of o-Benzoquinone Intermediates.
title: What roasting a beef patty does to its proteins
blurb: Roasted beef patty structure governs both oxidative stability and protein cross-linking at once, with o-benzoquinone intermediates floated as the likely link between the two. Mechanistic food chemistry, not a cooking tip.

original_title: Reduced Lutetium-177 PSMA Activity Matches Standard Regimen Efficacy in Prostate Cancer Study - Bioengineer.org
title: A smaller Lu-177 PSMA dose, same result
blurb: A reduced activity of Lutetium-177 PSMA therapy matched the standard regimen's efficacy in a prostate cancer study. If that holds up, it's less radiation for the same outcome, which is the kind of result worth not overselling until there's more behind it than one study.

original_title: Ligand-Controlled Chemodivergent β-Methylene C(sp3)–H Heteroarylation of Aliphatic Acids
title: Two ligands, two different couplings, same aliphatic acid
blurb: A Pd(II)-catalyzed beta-methylene C(sp3)-H heteroarylation where swapping between two classes of bidentate pyridone ligand steers free aliphatic acids to different products on demand. They also happen to fix the old problem where heteroaryl iodides just killed the reaction, which makes this look like a genuinely general C(sp3)-C(sp2) coupling route from cheap acids.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Triethylamine Concentration as a Molecular Switch for Chemodivergent Asymmetric Hydrogenation of Quinolinyl Ketones via Ru/Rh–Diamine Catalysis
title: One triethylamine knob picks which chiral alcohol you get
blurb: Same Ru/Rh-diamine catalyst, same quinolinyl ketone, but dial the triethylamine loading and the catalyst chirality and the hydrogenation steers toward either the quinoline alcohol or the fully reduced tetrahydroquinoline alcohol, both up to 99% ee. Runs at gram scale, so it's not just a flask curiosity.

original_title: Dynamic total body PET/CT after oral [18F]FDG administration
title: FDG PET, no injection required
blurb: Total body PET/CT done dynamically after an oral dose of FDG instead of the usual IV push. If oral dosing holds up kinetically, that's one less needle for a scan people already tolerate poorly enough.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Photosensitized Intermolecular Transposed TTEnT-Single-Electron Transfer Paternò-Büchi Reaction between Densely Substituted Styrenes and Aryl Aldehydes
title: A new route to Paternò-Büchi for styrenes too crowded to do it the normal way
blurb: Visible-light photocatalysis pairs triplet energy transfer with a single-electron-transfer twist to run the Paternò-Büchi cycloaddition between heavily substituted styrenes and aryl aldehydes, apparently a first for styrenes this crowded. It leans on their strong reducing character to get there, so it reads as a mechanism proof more than a broad scope paper yet.

original_title: Antibody-Aptamer Cooperative Enhanced Recognition and Ion-Mediated DNA Nanosphere for Rapid Monitoring of Mesenchymal CTCs
title: Antibody and aptamer team up to catch the CTCs that slip through alone
blurb: A DNA nanosphere held together by Ag+-mediated C-Ag+-C pairing, decorated with both an aptamer and an antibody so the two binding modes work the same target cooperatively instead of separately. The point is turning rare mesenchymal CTC binding events into an actual measurable signal, which is usually where these assays lose sensitivity.

original_title: A Bioinspired Thiolate-Bridged Diiron System for Functionally Replicating Hydrazine Dehydrogenase and Its Efficient Electrocatalytic Hydrazine Oxidation
title: A synthetic stand-in for hydrazine dehydrogenase that also doubles as a fuel cell catalyst
blurb: A thiolate-bridged diiron complex built to mimic hydrazine dehydrogenase, the anammox enzyme that turns hydrazine into N2 by a mechanism nobody's actually pinned down. Molecular electrocatalysts for hydrazine oxidation are rare since the field runs mostly on heterogeneous systems, so a well-defined diiron complex that does the chemistry efficiently is the notable part, with the fuel cell angle as a bonus.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: A Bowl-Shaped B,N-Tetraquinane Organic Super-Reductant
title: The strongest organic reductant yet, and it's shaped like a bowl
blurb: A bowl-shaped B-N tetraquinane made in one high-yield step hits -3.2 V vs Fc/Fc+, a new record among organic reductants. The voltage isn't just a number on a CV trace either: it drives [3+2] cycloadditions with ketones and imines, dearomatizes phthalazine, cleaves strong C-Si bonds, and reduction-borylates fluorobenzene, so the reducing power comes with reaction scope attached.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Cation Pinning toward High-Concentration Formic Acid Fuel Cells
title: Formic acid fuel cells don't choke on CO, they choke on pH
blurb: Concentrated formic acid fuel cells lose power as fuel concentration climbs, and CO poisoning usually takes the blame. This one pins it on interfacial acid-base kinetics instead, then fixes it by anchoring OH- at rare-earth-oxide-modified Rh single-atom sites to force a localized pH inversion at the interface. Reassigning the actual failure mode is the real finding, the Rh sites are just how they proved it.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Visible light mediated reactivity scope of hypervalent iodine reagents
title: A tour of what visible light does to hypervalent iodine reagents
blurb: A survey of PIDA, PIFA, and benziodoxole-type hypervalent iodine(III) reagents run under visible-light photoredox, covering their oxidation, functionalization, and group-transfer chemistry. Reads as a scope overview rather than one new reaction, so don't expect a single headline result here.

original_title: Ring‐Retaining Polymerization of Vinylidenecyclopropanes
title: Vinylidenecyclopropanes finally polymerize without blowing the ring open
blurb: VDCPs normally polymerize by ring-opening because of their butatriene character, while the allene-type mode that keeps the cyclopropane ring intact had stayed out of reach. An organonickel catalyst with the right coordinating counterion pulls off that ring-retaining polymerization instead, leaving pendant alkylidenecyclopropane groups on the backbone, which computations trace to strain-release alkene coordination.

original_title: Systematic evaluation of energy window and reconstruction parameters for quantitative lutetium-177 SPECT imaging on a CZT-based starguide SPECT/CT system.
title: Tuning the knobs on Lu-177 SPECT quantification
blurb: A systematic run through energy window and reconstruction settings for quantitative Lu-177 SPECT on the CZT-based StarGuide system. Dosimetry for Lu-177 therapy lives or dies on getting these calibration details right, so it's the unglamorous but necessary kind of paper.

original_title: Electrochemical PVC Recycling Unlocks Efficient Ring‐Closure Toward Amine‐Bearing Ketene Acetals as Novel Monomers for Poly(Amino Ester) Synthesis
title: PVC recycling makes its own monomer out of the chlorine it strips off
blurb: A paired electrochemical setup dechlorinates the PVC backbone at one electrode while the freed chloride gets built into cyclic halo acetals at the other. Those get converted to ketene acetals and ring-opened into degradable polyesters and amine-bearing poly(amino ester)s. The trick is using the waste stream as the feedstock instead of just scrubbing it out.

original_title: Serial [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 PET/MRI during teprotumumab therapy in thyroid eye disease
title: Tracking thyroid eye disease with FAPI PET while teprotumumab does its work
blurb: Serial Ga-68 FAPI-04 PET/MRI scans taken through a course of teprotumumab for thyroid eye disease, presumably to see whether fibroblast activation tracks the clinical response. Thin on detail beyond that.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Rhodium(III)-Catalyzed [4 + 3] Annulation of Indole-/Pyrrole-2-carboxamides with Propargyl Carbonates: Access to Seven-Membered Indolo/Pyrroloazepinones
title: Rhodium stitches indole carboxamides into seven-membered azepinones
blurb: Rh(III)-catalyzed C–H allenylation/annulation couples indole- and pyrrole-2-carboxamides with propargyl carbonates to build seven-membered indolo/pyrroloazepinone rings in one step. Redox-neutral, regioselective, and the functional group tolerance is broad, which is usually the part that kills these annulations.

original_title: Bioinspired Ångström-Scale Coupling of Reductive Centers in Covalent Organic Frameworks Drives Efficient Photocatalytic Oxygen Reduction
title: Packing a COF's reduction sites atom-close, enzyme style
blurb: Borrowing the trick multimetal enzyme centers use, these ortho-amino COFs cram several reductive sites into sub-nanometer catalytic pockets so they can cooperatively grab O2 and pass electrons around for photocatalytic oxygen reduction. The spacing is the whole point, not just a denser catalyst.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Sequence-dependent structural propensities of low complexity peptides accessed by automated flow synthesis
title: Flow-synthesized peptides map how low-complexity sequences fold
blurb: Automated fast-flow synthesis churned out ten peptides built from restricted amino acid sets across three repeat architectures. ATR-FTIR turns up a mix of beta-turn and beta-sheet signatures, and AlphaFold 2 versus 3 agree with the data to different degrees depending on the sequence. More a structure-prediction stress test than a discovery.

original_title: Enantioselective C(sp 3)–C(sp 3) Radical Coupling Through Photoinduced Electron Donor–Acceptor Activation
title: Pairing two short-lived radicals without losing the chirality
blurb: Two separate EDA photoactivation events each spin up an alkyl radical, and a chiral nickel catalyst couples them enantioselectively to make alpha-fluoroalkylated secondary alcohols. Controlling one transient radical is hard enough; doing it for two at once in a chiral pocket is the actual feat here.

original_title: Tryptophan-Based Imaging Agents for Major Depressive Disorders.
title: A tryptophan-based tracer for imaging depression
blurb: Imaging agents built on tryptophan, aimed at major depressive disorder. Not much more to go on than that.

original_title: Tetrahydro-Dewar Pyridines: Rigidified Piperidines for Drug Discovery
title: Dewar pyridines as stiffened piperidine scaffolds
blurb: Tetrahydro-Dewar pyridines proposed as rigidified versions of the piperidine ring that shows up everywhere in drug discovery. Not much detail beyond the pitch.

original_title: Photoredox/nickel dual-catalyzed C–N cross-coupling using P/N-heteroleptic copper as a photocatalyst
title: A copper photocatalyst fills in for iridium in C–N coupling
blurb: Photoredox/nickel dual catalysis couples aryl iodides with anilines to make diarylamines, but the photocatalyst here is an earth-abundant P/N-heteroleptic copper complex instead of the usual precious-metal one. Runs milder than the classic thermal routes and claims to sort out chemoselectivity among competing reactive groups, which is normally where these couplings trip up.

original_title: Chiral Bicyclic Secondary Amine Organocatalysts Featuring Bridgehead Carbons Adjacent to Nitrogen: Design, Synthesis, and Catalytic Applications
title: New bicyclic amine catalysts built to dodge their own death trap
blurb: Secondary amine organocatalysts usually die by forming an irreversible imine with the electrophile they're supposed to be activating. These bicyclic versions put a bridgehead carbon right next to the nitrogen to block that, made in six steps from a commercial epoxide and chiral amine, and used for asymmetric alpha-amination of alpha,alpha-disubstituted aldehydes.

original_title: Regio‐ and Stereoselective Carbotrifluoromethylation of Aryl Acetylenes Through Syn ‐Carboboration
title: One Cu catalyst, two steps to β-CF3 styrenes
blurb: Cu-catalyzed syn-carboboration of aryl acetylenes sets up a vinylborate that then gets trifluoromethylated with Ruppert-Prakash reagent, or pentafluoroethylated, landing β-CF3 styrenes with sharp regio- and stereocontrol under mild conditions. A tidy way to put the CF3 exactly where you want it instead of wherever the alkyne feels like putting it.

original_title: Palladium-Catalyzed TMM-Based Annulation Reactions: Mechanistic Manifolds and C–C, C–N, and C–O Bond Formation
title: A map of what Pd-TMM chemistry can actually build
blurb: A review that sorts palladium-TMM annulations by mechanism rather than by product: sequential double allylic substitution of bis-allylic electrophiles, classic zwitterionic Pd-TMM cycloadditions, and decarboxylative aza/oxa-π-allylpalladium dipole routes, covering C-C, C-N, and C-O bond formation. Useful if you want the mechanistic lay of the land rather than a parts catalog of heterocycles.

original_title: Harnessing a Recyclable Choline Chloride–Boric Acid Deep Eutectic Solvent for Sustainable One‐Pot Synthesis of Substituted Pyridines
title: A deep eutectic solvent that builds pyridines and gets reused
blurb: A choline chloride/boric acid deep eutectic solvent runs a metal-free, one-pot, three-component pyridine synthesis from aldehydes, acetophenones, and ammonium acetate, with the mix's Lewis acidity and hydrogen-bonding doing the catalytic work. The recyclability is the whole pitch, assuming it actually survives as many runs as these papers always promise.

original_title: Ru(II)‐Catalyzed C‐H Allylation of 1,2,3‐Benzotriazinones With Allyl Methyl Carbonate and Ethylene Carbonate
title: Ru(II) C-H allylation puts the allyl group right where the directing group points
blurb: Ru(II)-catalyzed, directed C-H allylation of 1,2,3-benzotriazinones using allyl methyl carbonate or ethylene carbonate as the allyl source, with the triazinone itself acting as the directing group. Broad substrate scope and good functional group tolerance, with yields reported up to 95%.

original_title: Targeted Degradation of the c-Myc Oncoprotein: Molecular Mechanisms, Technological Platforms, and Therapeutic Perspectives in Oncology.
title: Degrading c-Myc: still chemistry's favorite impossible target
blurb: A review of the mechanisms and technology platforms behind targeted degradation of the c-Myc oncoprotein, plus where the therapeutic case currently stands. c-Myc has been called undruggable for decades, so this is really a progress report on whether degraders are the thing that finally cracks it.

original_title: Cooperative Lewis Acid/Photoredox Catalysis for the Construction of Chiral Bicyclo[2.1.1]Hexanes
title: Photoredox plus a chiral Lewis acid builds bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes with real stereocontrol
blurb: Cooperative Lewis acid/photoredox catalysis runs an enantioselective strain-release [2σ+2π] annulation of bicyclobutanes with activated alkenes to make chiral BCHs, which are prized as stand-ins for ortho- and meta-substituted benzene rings. An acyl imidazole auxiliary anchors the bicyclobutane to a chiral lanthanide, lowering its reduction potential and organizing the stereochemistry. Enantioselective access to these benzene mimics has apparently been the sticking point, so that's the actual news here.

original_title: Pyrimidylsulfones as Condition-Responsive Sulfonyl Donors for Hydrosulfonylation
title: One sulfonyl donor, two mechanisms depending on which knob you turn
blurb: Bench-stable pyrimidylsulfones hand a sulfonyl group to electron-deficient alkenes two different ways from the same bottle: DMAP triggers an ionic Michael-type addition through an in-situ sulfinate, while visible-light photocatalysis with eosin Y runs the identical precursor through a radical Giese pathway instead. Metal-free either way, and the condition-responsive switch is the actual trick.

original_title: Access to the F-Ring Core of Viridicatumtoxin A via Decarboxylative Alkylation of Methylenetetracyclines at the C6 Position
title: Building toward viridicatumtoxin A's F-ring with a decarboxylative radical shortcut
blurb: Visible-light decarboxylative alkylation installs alkyl groups at C6 of methylenetetracyclines in one step while aromatizing the C-ring, using radical precursors from primary, secondary, and tertiary carboxylic acids, and it tolerates amides and free alcohols on the tetracycline substrate. It reaches the F-ring core of viridicatumtoxin A and the isopentenyl fragment of hypomycetin, and apparently threw in an unexpected oxa-7-membered ring along the way.

original_title: Unraveling the Location-Dependent Roles of C60 on Cu/SiO2 for Low-Pressure Hydrogenation of CO2-Derived Ethylene Carbonate to Methanol and Ethylene Glycol
title: Fullerenes on copper make CO2-derived carbonate hydrogenation easier on the H2 tank
blurb: A Cu/SiO2 catalyst loaded with multilayer C60 fullerenes hydrogenates CO2-derived ethylene carbonate to methanol and ethylene glycol at just 0.5 MPa H2 and 180°C, with the optimized 15C60-Cu/SiO2 version hitting near-complete conversion. The point is dodging the high H2 pressures that have kept this indirect CO2-to-methanol route impractical, and where the C60 sits on the catalyst turns out to matter.

original_title: Intracameral Injection of a Photocrosslinkable Methacrylated Hyaluronic Acid Hydrogel to Establish a Mouse Model of Chronic Ocular Hypertension.
title: A light-cured hydrogel gives mice a glaucoma model on demand
blurb: A single intracameral injection of methacrylated hyaluronic acid, crosslinked in place with light, raises intraocular pressure enough to establish a mouse model of chronic ocular hypertension. It's a research tool for studying glaucoma, not a treatment for it.

original_title: From Thermal to Electrochemical C═O Reduction Catalysis at Mn Complexes: Why Do Some Ligands Perform Better Than Others?
title: Mn pincer catalysts that ace carbonyl reduction on the bench, flop at the electrode
blurb: Mn PNP pincers are some of the best thermal carbonyl hydrogenation catalysts around, but almost nobody's run them electrochemically, where Mn-bipyridine still rules. Turns out there's a reason: the pincers only reduce at punishingly negative potentials because the redox-innocent PNP backbone barely takes up any electron density. A good explanation for why bipyridine keeps winning there, not a fix for it.

original_title: The power of O vacancies in electrocatalysis
title: Oxygen vacancies, now a dial instead of a dice roll
blurb: Electrocatalytic selectivity in non-stoichiometric oxides comes down to unpaired electrons trapped in oxygen vacancies, and getting a controlled number of them has mostly been luck. This synthesis uses template chemicals to set that count on purpose, which is the kind of lever this chemistry has been missing.

original_title: Selective Gas‐Phase Photocatalytic Methane‐to‐Methanol Conversion Over Gallium Oxynitride With Molecular Oxygen as the Sole Oxidant
title: Methane to methanol, running on plain room air
blurb: Methane-to-methanol photocatalysis usually self-destructs because the same conditions that activate methane also torch the methanol once it's made. This Ag/GaON/GaN catalyst gets around it, hitting 2.6 mmol/g/h at roughly 85% selectivity with O2, and it kept going when they swapped in untreated room air instead of pure oxygen in a closed loop. That air tolerance is the part worth noting, since that's what matters outside a gas cylinder.

original_title: Balanced Hydroxyl Binding Enables Productive Oxygen Transfer in Photocatalytic Benzene Hydroxylation
title: Getting more than a token yield out of photocatalytic benzene-to-phenol
blurb: Most routes to phenol via photocatalytic oxidation obsess over making hydroxyl radicals and ignore what happens once they're stuck to the surface, which is usually where the yield dies. Tuning the Pd site so hydroxyl species actually bind and turn over on WO3 gets PdOx/WO3 to 72.3% benzene conversion and 60.1% phenol yield at 83.1% selectivity under 420 nm light in water and air. Nowhere near displacing the cumene process on scale, but that selectivity for a radical-mediated oxidation is genuinely decent.

original_title: Assembly of Trifluoromethyl-Substituted Dihydrobenzoimidazo[2,1- b ]thiazoles via Cascade Annulation of 2-Mercaptobenzimidazoles with CF3-Imidoyl Sulfoxonium Ylides
title: A metal-free route to CF3-tagged benzimidazothiazoles
blurb: A [3+2] annulation stitches 2-mercaptobenzimidazoles together with CF3-imidoyl sulfoxonium ylides to build trifluoromethylated dihydrobenzoimidazothiazoles, no metal catalyst required. Comes with the usual methods-paper language about broad scope and mild conditions, so it's worth seeing how it holds up once someone outside the group runs an awkward substrate through it.

original_title: Domain Architecture Analysis Guides the Discovery of Unusual Glycyl Radical Enzyme Fusion Proteins
title: Mapping glycyl radical enzyme sequence space turns up an odd fusion
blurb: GREs handle a lot of the hard chemistry in anaerobic metabolism using a post-translationally installed glycyl radical, but the superfamily is so sequence-diverse that most of it has never been characterized. Sorting it with a sequence similarity network and then checking domain architecture cluster by cluster turns up an unexpected glycyl radical enzyme fusion protein. The sorting method is the real contribution, since it's what makes a cluster like that findable at all.

original_title: Programmable Skeletal Editing of Pyridines Into Regiodefined N ‐Alkyl Pyrazoles
title: Turning pyridines into pyrazoles by deleting two carbons
blurb: N-alkyl pyrazoles show up everywhere in drugs and agrochemicals, but making just one regioisomer by directly alkylating NH-pyrazoles is a crapshoot. This skeletal-editing route sidesteps that: install the N-substituent on a pyridine first, then run it through Zincke-type ring opening, acid-promoted cyclization, and a retro-Mannich that extrudes a two-carbon enamine. The regiochemistry ends up fixed by construction instead of by luck.

original_title: Temporal changes in FAPI uptake in subcutaneous U87MG xenografts progression: implications for preclinical FAP-targeted imaging and therapy.
title: FAPI uptake drifts as the tumor grows, which matters for dosing
blurb: Tracked FAPI uptake over time in subcutaneous U87MG xenografts as the tumors progressed, aimed at what that means for timing FAP-targeted imaging and therapy. If uptake meaningfully shifts across tumor stages, that's a scheduling problem for anyone planning a scan or a dose around it.
venue: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

original_title: Protein-interactions-guided peptide design for selective electrochemical detection of Salmonella typhimurium
title: Biosensor peptides lifted straight from a protein's own interfaces
blurb: Rather than raise an antibody, this grabs peptides directly from the interfaces a target protein already uses to recognize itself and its partners. For spotting Salmonella typhimurium, that's two peptides pulled off the needle protein PrgI, one from its self-oligomerization interface and one from where it binds its actual partner, wired into an electrochemical sensor. The structural logic is the selling point, not the electrode.

original_title: Acidity-Controlled Reduction Level and Porous Architecture of Graphene Hydrogels via Zn-Induced Interfacial Gelation.
title: Tuning graphene hydrogels with pH instead of harsher reducing agents
blurb: Zn-induced interfacial gelation builds graphene hydrogels where acidity controls both how reduced the graphene ends up and how porous the resulting network is, letting one variable do two jobs in making these gels tunable.

original_title: Single-Atom Cerium Unlocks Efficient Hydrogen Spillover within Nonreducible Zeolites through a Proton–Electron Relay
title: Cerium atoms give zeolites a hydrogen relay system
blurb: Single Ce atoms dropped into Pt/USY turn an otherwise inert zeolite support into an active hydrogen-transport medium, coupling proton and electron transfer instead of leaving spillover to chance. Backed by in situ spectroscopy, isotope tracing, and DFT. Nonreducible zeolites finally get an actual pathway instead of relying on whatever stray defects happen to be around.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Spatially Decoupled Cu-ZnO Mitigates Water-Acetylene Competitive Adsorption for Selective Acetylene Semihydrogenation
title: Keeping water off the active site so acetylene actually gets hydrogenated
blurb: Rather than cramming water activation and acetylene hydrogenation onto the same copper sites and hoping they don't interfere, this splits the two jobs across Cu and ZnO. Operando EIS and FTIR show ZnO preferentially mopping up water, which is apparently enough to kill the competitive adsorption that usually wrecks selectivity.

original_title: Visible‐Light Aerobic Upcycling of Polystyrene Enabled by a Thiadiazine‐Based Organophotocatalyst
title: Turning polystyrene into benzoic acid with blue light and air
blurb: A thiadiazine organophotocatalyst, pulled out of a screen of heterocycles, breaks polystyrene down to benzoic acid under a cheap 440 nm LED using air as the oxidant, no metal involved. It works on off-the-shelf commercial resins too, which is the part that matters if this is ever going to touch real plastic waste.

original_title: Photocatalytic PVDF Degradation Coupled With Catalytic Targeted Li Replenishment Toward Low‐Energy Repair of Spent LiFePO 4 Electrodes
title: Fixing dead LFP electrodes with light instead of a furnace
blurb: TiO2 under UV generates holes that drive •OH radicals to chew through the spent electrode's PVDF binder, and the authors pair that with targeted lithium replenishment to repair LiFePO4 without the usual high-temperature resintering. Battery recycling's dirty work handed to a photocatalyst instead of heat.

original_title: Phosphate backbone epitranscriptomics: Discovery of natural RNA phosphorothioates and their writer machinery
title: Archaea are writing chemical marks straight onto the RNA backbone
blurb: Not a base or sugar modification this time, the mark sits on the phosphate itself. Esti enzymes install these phosphorothioates at conserved rRNA and tRNA hotspots in anaerobic archaea, and the modified tRNAs hold up better at high growth temperatures. A whole new epitranscriptomic mark nobody had catalogued.

original_title: First-in-class RIPTAC tears into phase III trial
title: First RIPTAC drug makes it to phase III
blurb: Whatever you think of the acronym, this is the first RIPTAC to reach phase III, a first for the mechanism. No efficacy numbers yet, just the milestone of getting there.

original_title: Boosting DMF Electrosynthesis Over Bifunctional NiCo Catalysts via Methanol‐Supplemented *CHO Supply
title: A NiCo catalyst tops off DMF electrosynthesis with extra *CHO from methanol
blurb: Electrodeposited bifunctional NiCo makes DMF by electrosynthesis instead of the usual high-temperature, high-pressure route, hitting 56% Faradaic efficiency and 518 µmol cm⁻² h⁻¹ by feeding the *CHO intermediate with supplemental methanol. Decent numbers for a reaction that's normally brute-forced with heat.

original_title: Helicity Amplification in a Stereodynamic Oxahelicene–Bisporphyrin Tweezer Enables Quantitative Chiral Sensing
title: A porphyrin tweezer that only goes chiral when it's actually holding something
blurb: On its own the oxahelicene-bridged bisporphyrin shows no CD signal, its P and M helices flipping too fast to tell apart. Chiral diamines binding the zinc porphyrin centers lock that equilibrium to one helicity, turning simple molecular recognition into an amplified, quantitative chiroptical readout.

original_title: Bayer becomes latest Big Pharma to head to Hansoh in $3.3B deal for phase 1 ADC
title: Bayer gets in line for Hansoh's ADCs, $3.3B for one phase 1 asset
blurb: Bayer is the latest Big Pharma name to pay up for antibody-drug conjugate rights out of Hansoh, following the rest of the industry down the same well-worn path to the same Chinese ADC shop.

original_title: Functionalized Magnetic Covalent Organic Framework for High-Performance Isolation of Extracellular Vesicles Enables Burden-Free Monitoring of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
title: A magnetic COF that pulls exosomes out of a few drops of plasma
blurb: Annexin V grafted onto a magnetic covalent organic framework isolates extracellular vesicles from microvolume plasma without the large blood draws or vesicle damage current methods need. Aimed at lupus biomarker monitoring, the point being proteomics-grade EVs without needing a full tube of blood.

original_title: Therapy-Dependent Modulation of Fibroblast Activation Protein Expression in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: Implications for FAP-Targeted Radiopharmaceutical Therapy.
title: Chemo changes how much FAP there is to target
blurb: In pancreatic cancer, fibroblast activation protein expression shifts depending on what therapy the tumor's already had, which matters a lot if you're planning to dose a FAP-targeted radiopharmaceutical afterward. Timing the scan or the treatment to the therapy history, not just the diagnosis, seems to be the point.

original_title: Utilization of an Activity-Based Probe to Explore Interactomes of DXP Synthase.
title: Fishing for DXP synthase's binding partners with an activity-based probe
blurb: An activity-based probe used to pull out whatever proteins actually associate with DXP synthase in cells. DXS runs the non-mevalonate pathway that bacteria and parasites rely on and humans don't, so its interactome is the kind of thing you'd want mapped before designing inhibitors around it.

original_title: Recent Advances in Stimuli-Responsive Hydrogels for Inflammatory Bowel Disease Therapy.
title: A roundup of smart hydrogels for IBD
blurb: A review tour of stimuli-responsive hydrogels being developed for inflammatory bowel disease, mechanisms and all. Survey piece, no new data of its own.

original_title: Glass‐Tube‐Microreactor Integration of Transition‐Metal‐Substituted Perovskite Nanocrystals for Enhanced Photocurrent and Photocatalytic Kinetics with Photon Management
title: Doping lead-halide perovskites with Fe and Co to speed up photocatalysis
blurb: Fe- and Co-substituted CsPbBr3 nanocrystals run through a glass-tube microreactor give steadier photocurrent switching and faster photocatalytic degradation. The doping measurably distorts the lattice, and modeling says Pb-site substitution by Fe or Co is a plausible way it's happening. Still a lead halide perovskite, so the usual stability caveats apply.

original_title: Bio-Based Adhesives Through the Lens of Crosslinking Chemistry: Mechanisms, Feedstock Compatibility, Performance and Industrial Status.
title: What's actually holding bio-based adhesives together, chemically
blurb: A review working through the crosslinking chemistry behind bio-based adhesives: which mechanisms are used, which feedstocks they're compatible with, how they perform, and where the industry actually stands. Survey, not a new adhesive.

original_title: Rational Regulation of Ligand Conformation Toward Topology Reconfiguration for Sieving Butane Isomers
title: A MOF tuned by ligand twist to sort n-butane from isobutane in one step
blurb: Changing the ligand's conformation reconfigures the whole MOF topology, turning the pillar-layer SIFSIX-TEPE-Cu into a new cage-like SIFSIX-TEPH-Cu with a tighter, confined pore. That pore sieves n-C4H10 from its branched isomer by size alone while still holding a lot of n-butane and loading it fast, doing in one step what usually takes distillation.

original_title: Heteroleptic Neutral Iron(II) Complexes Based on a Doubly Deprotonated Tridentate 1,2,4-Triazole Ligand Showing Tunable Abrupt Spin Transitions Associated with Crystallographic Symmetry Breaking
title: Swapping one substituent to tune when an iron complex flips its spin state
blurb: Three heteroleptic Fe(II) complexes, built from the same triazole ligand paired with bpp, bppMe, or bppF, show abrupt spin transitions whose sharpness tracks a crystallographic symmetry-breaking that shifts with the substituent. They also lose solvent on filtration and take it back up on exposure, reversibly, so the spin switching and the solvation state are tangled together.

original_title: Moderate Pressures of H2 Enhance the Tandem Upcycling of Polyethylene to Alkylbenzenes
title: Turning plastic bags into surfactant feedstock, faster with a little H2
blurb: A Pt/SiO2-Al2O3 catalyst breaks down waste polyethylene into alkylbenzenes, the stuff anionic surfactants are made from, at around 280°C with no hydrogen required. Add 1-8 bar of H2 anyway and the rate jumps, peaking near 4 bar, right where the thermodynamics said it should. Recycled-carbon surfactants instead of petrochemical ones, if the catalyst survives real feedstock.

original_title: DosePET: An Open-Source Dataset with 2100 Radiation Dose Maps for PET/CT
title: 2,100 Monte Carlo dose maps, free, for anyone training dosimetry AI
blurb: An open dataset of patient-specific absorbed-dose maps built by Monte Carlo simulation: 1,503 FDG scans plus 597 PSMA scans (PSMA-1007 and Ga-PSMA-11) pulled from five institutions and seven scanner models. Unglamorous, but it's exactly the kind of bulk labeled data that personalized dosimetry AI has been short on.

original_title: Monte Carlo-based secondary dose check platform for the world's first ultra-compact upright proton therapy system
title: An independent dose check for the first upright proton therapy machine
blurb: A TOPAS Monte Carlo model of the Mevion S250-FIT's nozzle, energy modulator, and adaptive aperture, commissioned against measured depth-dose curves and spot profiles across 12 energy settings, built to cross-check RayStation's own treatment plans. Standard due diligence, just for a machine whose upright, ultra-compact geometry is genuinely new.

original_title: Revealing hidden dynamics in steady-state heterogeneous catalysis through photon-statistical spectroscopy
title: "Steady" catalysis might be quietly oscillating after all
blurb: Bulk measurements make a heterogeneous catalytic reaction look like it's settled into steady state, but photon-statistics spectroscopy digs into the fluctuations and finds collective dynamical organization underneath, the same kind of self-sustained oscillation usually reserved for CO oxidation as the textbook example. Experimentally confirmed cases of this kind of temporal organization in catalysis are rare, so if this generalizes, a lot of reactions we call steady-state might just be oscillating faster than anyone bothered to look.

original_title: Integrating Enzymatic Catalysis and Photocatalysis with Covalent Organic Frameworks
title: COFs playing matchmaker between enzymes and photocatalysts
blurb: A review rounding up covalent organic frameworks that double as the photocatalyst and as a protective shell around the enzyme in the same system, the point being you get both halves of the catalysis working together instead of bolted on separately. It covers how the coupling actually happens, cofactor-mediated, H2O2-mediated, radical-mediated, direct electron transfer, and photo-driven routes, which is useful as a map of the field but it's a survey piece, not a new result.
